description: Two slope generators, each one a slew limiter, an envelope and an oscillator depending on what is patched into it

params.text: Sets how long the slope takes to rise, from instant at one end to several seconds at the other
Attenuverts what modulates the rise time, -1 to +1
Sets how long the slope takes to fall, from instant at one end to several seconds at the other
Attenuverts what modulates the fall time, -1 to +1
Switches what modulates the rise time between the rise CV jacks and the slope's own output, which bends the straight ramp into a curve
Switches what modulates the fall time between the fall CV jacks and the slope's own output, which bends the straight ramp into a curve
Holds the slope cycling on its own, so it runs as an oscillator rather than waiting for a trigger

inputs.text: The signal the slope follows; it climbs towards it at the rise rate and drops towards it at the fall rate, which makes it a slew limiter or a lag
A trigger here fires one slope, up to 8V and back down to 0V
Scales both times by a volt per octave, which is what makes the cycling slope play as an oscillator
Modulates the rise time, -10V to +10V, scaled by the rise attenuverter
Modulates the fall time, -10V to +10V, scaled by the fall attenuverter
Modulates the rise and the fall time together, -10V to +10V, scaled by both attenuverters

outputs.text: 10V while the slope is above 5V, and 0V below it
10V while the slope is at rest, dropping to 0V for as long as it is rising or falling
The slope itself, 0V to 8V, or the slewed input when one is patched
The slope shifted down by 5V, so it swings either side of zero

inputs.1: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.7: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.8: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
